summary: The only occurrence was checked against the complete verse. It is the existing LuF 272/33 passage under the alternate text reference LuF 1/33, so no new lexical sense, stem, box or duplicate example is justified.

Source variant: supplied komʕazalle versus inherited ko-mʕazal-la. The following hiye koḥošawle supports the officer’s male construal of the disguised person, but source transcription variance is not excluded. No definitive fix-text is proposed without edition verification.

The mʕazər stem has r+l assimilation in the patient chain. This does not establish a different root. A person subject reprimands a person patient; the Arabic lexical loan is a finite verb, not a light-verb construction.
The supplied German Hann is retained as an edition/transcription irregularity and not silently rewritten as Mann. No added quotation reproduces the existing example merely to display this typo.
Does the edition at LuF 272/33 intentionally read masculine -le, reflecting the officer’s viewpoint, or does it read the inherited feminine -la? Compare the source before changing patient gender.
Confirm the LuF 1/33 versus LuF 272/33 text/page reference concordance and the supplied German Hann reading.
